origin: Codex 0.142.5: the only thing the relay writes is a tool call, and it runs out of tokens in the middle of its arguments (finish_reason length, as when the first action of a turn is to write a big file with one command). Codex names no output limit, so the limit is the gateway's own default (4096 tokens): the answer has no text and no whole call, and told as incomplete it would be asked for five more times, each paid for. The gateway holds the answer back (WITHHELD: a 502 that is not charged, and not a failure of the relay), the relay is kept from the session, and the client's retry reaches Kiro, which is held to the same 4096 tokens (design O12). The relay answers are authored from the documented Chat Completions shapes; the expected files are what the gateway does with them.
